analysis:
The only change in this PR for the supplied file is a comment edit at around line 4361 of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, where the comment now clarifies that SSDWriteBehind.consume charges the bucket per entry in array order only when the whole donation does not fit. That hunk lies outside the supplied text units, which cover lines 1756-3038. The supplied head text is existing test code covering the following:
- ready-receipt monotonicity and failure matrices
- write-behind barriers
- low-disk reserve, where the pending donation must fit above the reserve
- ENOSPC handling
- in-flight close outcomes
- staging-reservation hygiene against GlobalKVCacheBudget
- shared-entry tickets
- instance namespaces
- root isolation (kv3 sits outside the legacy kv root)
- whole-root maintenance (TTL, budget, epoch retention)

The change touches no production code, so no encryption, HMAC lookup-tag, TTL, KEK or authorization behavior is altered. I found no regression against T-041 or the related SSD cache mitigations. These tests assert the intended controls: fail-closed on corrupt blocks, no ready receipt on failure, reservations released on all paths, and the pending-donation free-space reserve. The comment edit mentions a pending-donation-fit behavior in SSDWriteBehind.consume, but the implementation of that behavior is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. Because this PR is test and comment only, I raise no integration concern. Any change to the SSDWriteBehind rate-limit semantics would need review in production source.
